narrative: Under a combined adverse scenario — ECB −100 bps, markets −20% and cost of risk at 150 bps — 12-month profit falls from EUR 62.8M to about EUR 21M but stays positive. The largest shocks are credit (EUR 22.2M) and fees (EUR 13.8M). The model puts the CET1 trough at about 19.1%, still 4.8 points above the overall capital requirement.

signals.title: CET1 down to 20.17% at June 2026
signals.excerpt: CET1 capital of €346.8M on €1,719M of risk-weighted assets; 5.9 points of headroom over the 14.28% overall capital requirement.

signals.title: Net fees now exceed net interest income
signals.excerpt: Net fees €91.6M vs NII €80.8M; gross fees +33% to €132.9M with Tressis and the Spanish bank in the perimeter.
